title: Chief Roi Mata's Domain
summary: Chief Roi Mata's Domain is a group of three sites on Efate, Lelepa and Artok in central Vanuatu tied to the life, death and burial of Roi Mata, last holder of the paramount chief title, who lived around 1600 AD and is remembered for social reforms that ended conflict. UNESCO inscribed it in 2008.

uncertainty.note: Both pages place Roi Mata around 1600 AD, within the early 17th century; the end is the present, since the tabu-protected sites survive.

where.modern_name: Efate, Lelepa and Artok islands, Shefa Province, Vanuatu (pin at the UNESCO property coordinates)
where.historical_name: Chief Roi Mata's domain, central Vanuatu, before European contact

importance.justification: Vanuatu's first World Heritage property, linking oral tradition and archaeology around a chief remembered for ending war.

sources.title: Chief Roi Mata's Domain (Vanuatu), ICOMOS evaluation no. 1280
sources.publisher: ICOMOS (advisory body evaluation hosted by UNESCO)

reviewer_note: The UNESCO page gives the coordinates as S17 37 41.05 E168 10 39.79, converted here to decimal degrees; the three sites lie within a few kilometres of each other, so the pin is a property-level point. Roi Mata's dates are traditional estimates (around 1600 AD) from oral tradition and archaeology.
